original_question: Obtain upper bounds for 1/|zeta'(rho)| as rho ranges over the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
target_in_paper: Theoretical Problems, Problem #3 (Nicol Leong): “Can we obtain upper bounds for 1/|ζ′(ρ)| as ρ runs over the nontrivial zeros of ζ(s)?”
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper’s official problem almost word-for-word. It has the correct object, namely the reciprocal derivative 1/|ζ′(ρ)|, the correct family of points, namely the nontrivial zeros ρ of the Riemann zeta function, and the correct scope, namely a pointwise upper-bound problem rather than an averaged moment problem.
missing_details: ρ should be defined explicitly as a nontrivial zero of ζ(s), i.e. a complex number ρ with ζ(ρ)=0 and 0<Re(ρ)<1.
To make 1/|ζ′(ρ)| finite for every such ρ and to match the paper’s immediate context, one should state the simple zeros conjecture (SZ), namely that all nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) are simple.
The quantifier should be made explicit: the problem is to bound |ζ′(ρ)|^{-1} for each such zero ρ as ρ varies, not to study only an average over zeros up to height T.
The phrase “upper bounds” is meant in the pointwise sense of controlling how small ζ′(ρ) can be at an individual zero.

If one wants a fully quantitative version, the parameter of the bound should be specified, typically the height |Im ρ| (or γ when ρ=β+iγ), although the paper itself does not prescribe a particular final shape for the bound.
refined_question: Assuming the simple zeros conjecture for the Riemann zeta function, obtain nontrivial pointwise upper bounds for |ζ′(ρ)|^{-1} as ρ ranges over the nontrivial zeros of ζ(s), that is, over all complex numbers ρ with ζ(ρ)=0 and 0<Re(ρ)<1.
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem #3 in the paper’s “Theoretical Problems” section. The surrounding context shows that the authors have the pointwise quantity 1/ζ′(ρ) in mind, not a moment over many zeros: immediately after Problem #3 they assume SZ, record an explicit formula for the modified Mertens sum M0(x) involving 1/(ρζ′(ρ)), and then give equation (1), an exact product formula for 1/ζ′(ρ). The accompanying discussion says the main obstacle is controlling how close one zero can be to its nearest neighbour. Your draft is therefore essentially correct, but it is not fully stand-alone until ρ is defined precisely and the simplicity assumption is stated explicitly.
